A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the pseudo-magnetic field in the graphene nanobubbles can be understood in the context of a gauge field theory.
the pseudo-magnetic field is the geometrically induced gauge potential in graphene and it is the geometrically constrained wave function which is the key to the computation of its magnitude.
the pseudo-magnetic field in the nanobubble is not a consequence of the strain in the underlying crystal lattice but rather a manifestation of the geometry of the surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pseudo-magnetic field strength can be computed from first principles and is not a mere fitting parameter.
the pseudo-magnetic field is a direct consequence of the three dimensional nature of the carriers and their confinement to a two dimensional surface.
the gauge field in the graphene nanobubbles is a direct consequence of the three dimensional nature of the wave function and is not due to any topological defect.
